meta.description: Statutory deadlines by pipeline. Each deadline has a federal baseline and optional state overrides. The engine calculates remaining days from the triggering event date.
meta.disclaimer: General guidance — not legal advice. Deadlines may vary by jurisdiction, case facts, and tolling provisions. Consult legal aid for time-sensitive matters.

federal.notes: No federal deadline — state law governs

WA.notes: No strict deadline. Temporary order issued same day; full hearing within 14 days.

OR.notes: No strict deadline. Temporary order ex parte; hearing within 21 days.

CA.notes: No strict deadline. TRO issued same day; hearing within 21-25 days.

deadlines.action: File police report for domestic violence incident

federal.notes: No federal deadline — report as soon as possible

WA.notes: Misdemeanor DV: 1 year. Felony DV: 3 years (RCW 9A.04.080).

OR.notes: Misdemeanor: 2 years. Felony: 3-6 years depending on class.

CA.notes: Misdemeanor: 1 year. Felony: 3 years. Aggravated DV: no limit.

federal.notes: Must file within 2 years of divorce from abuser. No deadline if still married.

deadlines.action: Respond to eviction notice / unlawful detainer

federal.notes: No federal deadline — state law governs

WA.notes: 20 days to respond to unlawful detainer summons. 14-day pay-or-vacate for nonpayment.

OR.notes: 7 days to appear after service. 72-hour notice for nonpayment (13 days if first offense).

CA.notes: 5 days to respond to unlawful detainer. 3-day pay-or-quit for nonpayment.

deadlines.action: File habitability complaint with code enforcement

federal.notes: No federal deadline — file after landlord fails to repair within reasonable time

WA.notes: Landlord has 10 days to begin repair after written notice. File complaint if no action within 30 days.

OR.notes: Landlord has 7 days for emergency repairs, 30 days for non-emergency. File after deadline passes.

CA.notes: Landlord has 30 days after notice. Tenant may repair-and-deduct or withhold rent after 30 days.

federal.notes: No federal deadline — state law governs

WA.notes: Landlord must return deposit or itemized deductions within 21 days.

OR.notes: Landlord has 31 days to return deposit with itemized statement.

CA.notes: Landlord has 21 days to return deposit with itemized statement. 2x penalty for bad faith.

federal.notes: File with HUD within 1 year of discriminatory act.

WA.notes: File with WSHRC within 1 year.

OR.notes: File with BOLI within 1 year.

CA.notes: File with CRD within 3 years (extended from 1 year in 2024).

deadlines.action: File internal appeal of claim denial

federal.notes: ERISA plans: 180 days for internal appeal. ACA plans: 180 days.

WA.notes: 180 days from denial. Insurer must respond within 30 days (urgent: 72 hours).

OR.notes: 180 days from denial. Insurer must respond within 30 days.

CA.notes: 180 days from denial. HMO: file with DMHC. PPO: file with CDI.

federal.notes: ACA: 4 months from internal appeal denial for external review.

WA.notes: 180 days from internal appeal denial. File with OIC for IRO review.

OR.notes: 180 days. File with DCBS for independent review.

CA.notes: HMO: 180 days for IMR through DMHC (free, binding). PPO: 180 days through CDI.

deadlines.action: File complaint with state insurance regulator

federal.notes: No federal deadline — file with state regulator anytime

WA.notes: No deadline. File with OIC anytime. OIC investigates within 30 days.

OR.notes: No deadline. File with DCBS anytime.

CA.notes: No deadline. HMO: DMHC (888-466-2219). PPO: CDI (800-927-4357).

federal.notes: State law governs SOL for bad faith claims

WA.notes: 3-year SOL for bad faith (contract) or CPA violation.

OR.notes: 6-year SOL for breach of contract / bad faith.

CA.notes: 2-year SOL for bad faith tort. 4 years for breach of written contract.

deadlines.action: File wage claim with state labor agency

federal.notes: FLSA: 2 years for non-willful, 3 years for willful violations.

WA.notes: 3 years. File with L&I. Double damages for willful violations.

OR.notes: 2 years. File with BOLI. Penalty wages up to 30 days.

CA.notes: 3 years for unpaid wages. File with DLSE (Labor Commissioner). 4 years for written contract.

federal.notes: No federal deadline — state law governs final pay timing

WA.notes: Due at next regular payday. Double damages if willfully withheld.

OR.notes: If fired: due by end of next business day. If quit with 48hr notice: due on last day.

CA.notes: If fired: due immediately. If quit with 72hr notice: due on last day. Waiting time penalty: up to 30 days' wages.

federal.notes: EEOC: 300 days in states with FEP agency. 180 days otherwise.

WA.notes: File with WSHRC within 300 days (worksharing with EEOC).

OR.notes: File with BOLI within 1 year.

CA.notes: File with CRD within 3 years (extended 2024). Worksharing with EEOC.

federal.notes: State law governs — typically 24-72 hours after removal

WA.notes: Shelter care hearing within 72 hours of removal (excluding weekends/holidays).

OR.notes: Shelter hearing within 24 hours (next judicial day).

CA.notes: Detention hearing within 48 hours of removal (next court day).

deadlines.action: Verify ICWA notice was properly sent to tribe

federal.notes: ICWA requires notice to tribe by registered mail. No specific day count but must be 'timely.' Tribe has 20 days to respond.

WA.notes: WA ICWA (WICWA) requires notice. Active efforts required, not just reasonable efforts.

OR.notes: OR ICWA requires notice. Must make active efforts to prevent breakup of Indian family.

CA.notes: CA ICWA requires inquiry at every hearing. Notice must be sent if reason to know child is AI/AN.

federal.notes: ASFA: permanency hearing within 12 months of removal. TPR petition if child in care 15 of last 22 months.

WA.notes: 12 months. Reunification services typically 6-12 months.

OR.notes: 12 months. Permanency plan required.

CA.notes: 6-month review + 12-month permanency hearing. 18 months max for reunification services.

deadlines.action: Dispute debt in writing after validation notice

federal.notes: FDCPA: 30 days to dispute in writing. Collector must cease until verified.

WA.notes: 30 days (follows FDCPA). WA Collection Agency Act provides additional protections.

OR.notes: 30 days (follows FDCPA). OR Unlawful Debt Collection Practices Act.

CA.notes: 30 days (follows FDCPA). Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act extends to original creditors.

federal.notes: 1 year from violation. Statutory damages up to $1,000 + actual damages + attorney fees.

WA.notes: 4 years for WA CPA violations. FDCPA: 1 year (federal).

OR.notes: 1 year for OR UDCPA. $200 statutory damages per violation.

CA.notes: 1 year for Rosenthal Act. Statutory damages up to $1,000.

deadlines.action: Assert statute of limitations defense on old debt

federal.notes: State law governs SOL on debt. Collector cannot sue on time-barred debt.

WA.notes: 6 years for written contracts. 3 years for oral contracts.

OR.notes: 6 years for written contracts. 6 years for oral contracts.

CA.notes: 4 years for written contracts. 2 years for oral contracts.

federal.notes: State law governs — typically 10-30 days after notice

WA.notes: Object within 20 days of notice. Right to counsel.

OR.notes: Object within 15 days of notice.

CA.notes: Object at or before hearing. Typically 15 days notice required.

federal.notes: State law governs — guardians typically must file annual reports

WA.notes: Guardian must file annual report within 90 days of anniversary. Court can remove for failure.

OR.notes: Annual report due within 30 days of anniversary.

CA.notes: Accounting due within 90 days of anniversary. Biennial for established guardianships.

deadlines.action: Report suspected elder abuse to APS

federal.notes: Elder Justice Act encourages reporting. No federal deadline — state law governs mandatory reporting.

WA.notes: Mandatory reporters: within 48 hours. Anyone can report. APS: 866-363-4276.

OR.notes: Mandatory reporters: immediately (within 24 hours). Anyone can report. APS: 855-503-7233.

CA.notes: Mandatory reporters: within 2 working days (phone report immediately). APS: 833-401-0832.

federal.notes: CMS requires states to investigate within 2-10 days depending on severity. No filing deadline.

WA.notes: No deadline. File with DSHS RCS (800-562-6078) or LTC Ombudsman (800-562-6028).

OR.notes: No deadline. File with DHS Aging & People with Disabilities or LTC Ombudsman (800-522-2602).

CA.notes: No deadline. File with CDPH (800-236-9747) or LTC Ombudsman (800-231-4024).

federal.notes: Report to APS and local law enforcement. Consider SAR filing if financial institution involved.

WA.notes: Financial institutions: report within 5 business days. Others: report to APS.

OR.notes: Same as abuse — mandatory reporters must report immediately.

CA.notes: Financial institutions: report within 2 business days. Others: report to APS.

deadlines.action: File motion to modify custody order

federal.notes: State law governs. Must show substantial change in circumstances.

WA.notes: No deadline but must show adequate cause. 2-year waiting period unless child's health at risk.

OR.notes: No deadline. Must show substantial change in circumstances.

CA.notes: No deadline. Must show changed circumstances. Emergency ex parte if child at risk.

federal.notes: State law governs appellate deadlines

WA.notes: 30 days from entry of order to file notice of appeal.

OR.notes: 30 days from entry of judgment.

CA.notes: 60 days from notice of entry of judgment. 180 days if no notice served.

deadlines.action: File contempt motion for custody order violation

federal.notes: No federal deadline — state law governs

WA.notes: No strict deadline. File promptly. Court can impose sanctions, modify custody.

OR.notes: No strict deadline. File promptly. Court can impose fines, jail, modify custody.

CA.notes: No strict deadline. File promptly. Court can impose fines up to $1,000, jail up to 5 days per violation.
